differences.title: 1. CORE FUNCTIONALITY
differences.leftDesc: Biome integrates linting, formatting, and more into a single, fast binary. It handles code style and potential errors with one unified engine.
differences.rightDesc: ESLint focuses on code quality and style rules, requiring a separate formatter like Prettier for code consistency. It's highly configurable.

differences.title: 2. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Biome is written in Rust, achieving near-instantaneous analysis and formatting speeds across projects. It compiles to a single binary for efficiency.
differences.rightDesc: ESLint, written in JavaScript, can be slower on large codebases. Its performance depends heavily on the number of plugins and rules configured.

differences.title: 3. CONFIGURATION
differences.leftDesc: Biome uses a unified `biome.json` file for all configurations, simplifying project setup and management. It aims for sensible defaults.
differences.rightDesc: ESLint often uses `.eslintrc.*` files, potentially leading to complex hierarchies and overrides. It offers granular control over every rule.

differences.title: 4. ECOSYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: Biome aims to be a complete developer toolchain, including formatter, linter, bundler, and potentially more, under one name and project.
differences.rightDesc: ESLint is a mature linter with a vast ecosystem of plugins and integrations for various frameworks and specific linting needs.

differences.title: 5. SUPPORTED LANGUAGES
differences.leftDesc: Biome currently focuses on JavaScript, TypeScript, and JSON, with plans for expansion. Its core is built for web technologies.
differences.rightDesc: ESLint supports JavaScript and TypeScript, with numerous community plugins enabling linting for HTML, Vue, React JSX, and other syntaxes.

differences.title: 6. ERROR REPORTING
differences.leftDesc: Biome provides detailed diagnostic messages with code actions, suggesting fixes directly within the terminal or editor integration.
differences.rightDesc: ESLint reports errors and warnings based on configured rules, often requiring manual intervention or external tools for automated fixes.

differences.title: 7. DEVELOPMENT PHILOSOPHY
differences.leftDesc: Biome strives for a cohesive and opinionated developer experience, reducing configuration overhead and ensuring consistent code quality.
differences.rightDesc: ESLint prioritizes flexibility and customization, allowing developers to tailor linting rules precisely to project needs and team preferences.
